items.reasons: The cabinet is drawn flat from the front: the pink top band is a front marquee, not a lit top plane seen from above, so the glass box shows no depth. The prizes inside are a cluttered patch of saturated sticker colours (yellow, pink, white) that lose their shapes at 1x.

The body is a near-black, low-contrast mass with only 2–3 dark grey steps, so it reads muddy next to the originals' clear light-to-dark shading. The orange pixels at the bottom (feet or pedals) look like detached bright specks under the cabinet.

A wall pegboard is drawn as a tall front-on panel standing in the middle of the floor; its only top surface is a thin plank and the face is a flat front view. The peg-hole dot grid and tiny product bottles make noisy speckle at 1x, and the big yellow '100' sign is a sticker-like block.

The pillar is a flat front view of a cylinder with no top cap seen from above. In the room it is a thin one-tile stub, far too small for a structural pillar. It sits loose in the middle of the floor with a flared base instead of reaching up to the wall or ceiling.

The facade is a pure front view with no floor or step plane. In the room it covers the back-wall band, and the awning sits on the wall stripe without lining up with the wall. Its footprint spills across both the wall and floor rows, so it reads as a pasted-on image rather than a shopfront set into the wall.

An overhead luggage rack is drawn as a floor-standing cabinet with three poster panels below. At 1x it reads as a notice board or vending unit, not a rack. The bag and box on the top bars are the only cue, and in the room it stands on the floor instead of being mounted high on the wall.
